# Data Ambiguity Strikes Back: How Documentation Improves GPT’s Text-to-SQL

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#data-ambiguity-documentation)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2310.18742v1) · arXiv:2310.18742v1, 28 October 2023; manuscript labeled Table Representation Learning Workshop at NeurIPS 2023

**Reading coverage:** All seven PDF pages: Sections 1-4, Table 1, Figure 1 panels and captions, limitations and references. No supplement or appendix in the PDF.

## Research question

A correctly interpreted question can still yield wrong SQL when the model misunderstands value formats, table coverage or row granularity.

## Method

The authors manually document two KaggleDBQA databases and clarify query terms/output schemas using supplied reference answers. They vary documentation content and query disambiguation separately, selecting relevant columns to reduce prompt redundancy.

## Evaluation

GPT-4 with an 8K context is evaluated on 45 Soccer/Crime questions, only two of KaggleDBQA’s eight databases. Exact-match evaluation is manually checked for equivalent formulations; the authors also repair inconsistent or faulty reference answers.

## What the results support

With queries already clarified, schema-only accuracy is 57.8% and full documentation reaches 86.7%: a 28.9-percentage-point gain. The original-question/schema-only condition is 26.7%, so these are different comparisons.

## Limits and qualifications

This is a small manually curated study. Gold-answer-guided documentation and question rewriting approximate oracle assistance, and missing-value semantics are left unresolved. No general automatic documentation or interactive clarification system is evaluated.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Shows why omitted data semantics should be distinguished from linguistic ambiguity and model generation errors.
